body.p: Status of the Application

By this Amendment, Claims 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7 have been amended for clarity, and Claim 5 has been canceled without prejudice or disclaimer. No new subject matter has been added. Claim 2 has been previously canceled. Thus, Claims 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7 are presently pending, with Claims 1, 6, and 7 being independent.
Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the claims in view of the presented amendments and accompanying remarks. Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 103

Claims 1 and 3-7 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as purportedly being unpatentable over Ratnasingam (US 9,672,734), in view of Abe (US 2019/0113914), and in further view of Watanabe (US 2018/0105185).
Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections for at least the following reasons and discusses independent Claim 1 as an example.
Without any admissions, independent Claim 1 has been amended to recite features similar to those previously recited in now-cancelled dependent Claim 5:
A vehicle control device configured to control a vehicle, comprising:
an information provision device configured to provide information to a
driver of the vehicle;

a processor, during automated driving control of the vehicle, configured to: perform the automated driving control by automatically performing a driving operation of the vehicle relating to an automated driving plan of the vehicle control device, the automated driving control comprising operations relating to at least one of acceleration, steering, and braking,
according to the automated driving plan;
provide, through the information provision device to the driver, a driving event that is to occur at a subsequent point ahead in a direction of
advance from a current point, based on the automated driving plan;

judge whether a driver driving operation being performed by the driver at the current point before the subsequent point of the driving event is acceptable to be performed, the driving event being a lane change to a first lane at a first side of the vehicle, the driver driving operation being a lane change to a second lane at the first side of the vehicle performed at the current point before the subsequent point of the driving event, the judging being based on whether the second lane is unable to be driven on between the current point and the subsequent point of the driving event due to at least one of a blockage or an ending of the second lane; and provide, through the information provision device to the driver, judgment information that causes the driver not to perform the driver driving operation, based on the judging that the driver driving operation is unacceptable according to the automated driving plan being executed by the vehicle control device, the judgment information comprising lane change inhibiting information indicating that the second lane is unable to be driven on between the current point and the subsequent point of the driving event due to the at least one of the blockage or the ending of the second lane, the judgment information further comprising distance information from the current point to a point where the second lane is unable to be driven due to the at least one of the blockage or the ending of the second lane.
At a minimum, the proposed Ratnasingam-Abe-Watanabe combination does not disclose,
teach, or suggest to "judge whether a driver driving operation being performed by the driver at the
current point before the subsequent point of the driving event is acceptable to be performed," and
"the judgment information [that is provided through the information provision device to the driver]
further comprising distance information from the current point to a point where the second lane is
unable to be driven due to the at least one of the blockage or the ending of the second lane", as
recited in Claim 1.
Ratnasingam is generally directed to "determining lane information in a road segment to
drive a first vehicle to minimize travel time." Ratnasingam, Abstract. In particular, Ratnasingam
discloses that " a change of lane may be required for the first vehicle to minimize travel time if the

other vehicle that is in the same lane and ahead of first vehicle is at least one from a list including currently parked, maneuvering to park, currently stopped, will stop ahead, stopped at blocked lane, broken down vehicle, vehicle stopped or will stop for loading or unloading or for some other reasons, waiting to turn, will turn from a lane in which the first vehicle is moving, a bus frequently stops, garbage collecting truck or other vehicle stops frequently, a vehicle moves slowly (non- limiting example: bicycle, vehicle driven by a learner driver, and slow vehicle in a fast moving motor way), and combinations thereof." Id. at col. 41, li. 19-31. Ratnasingam further discloses that "the server system may not present the determined lane if changing of the lane is difficult, other vehicles in the determined lane are close to the first vehicle, other conditions including driver's cognitive load or driver state prevent such an action, and vehicle conditions." Id. at col. 21, li. 56-61.

That is, at best, Ratnasingam discloses determining situations in which a change of lane may minimize travel time of a vehicle but not presenting those options if the changing of the lane is difficult.

To the extent the Office is attempting to equate the determined change of lane of Ratnasingam to the claimed "judging" features, Claim 1 recites to "judge whether a driver driving operation being performed by the driver at the current point before the subsequent point of the driving event is acceptable to be performed." Ratnasingam does not disclose judging any such operation, much less that the operation is being performed by the driver. Instead, at best, Ratnasingam discloses a server system that determines whether to present a determined lane change based on a difficulty of performing the lane change. Therefore, Ratnasingam's purported disclosure of a determined change of lane does not disclose claimed "judging" features. Consequently, Ratnasingam is unable to disclose or suggest to "judge whether a driver driving
operation being performed by the driver at the current point before the subsequent point of the driving event is acceptable to be performed," as recited in Claim 1.
The Office Action does not allege that Watanabe discloses the above-identified features of Claim 1 nor does Watanabe make up for at least these deficiencies of Ratnasingam.

In rejecting Claim 5, the Office Action acknowledges that Ratnasingam does not disclose that the judgment information comprises distance information as recited in Claim 1. See Office Action, p. 12 (citing Claim 5 prior to the present amendments). Instead, the Office Action relies on Watanabe as allegedly disclosing these features. Applicant respectfully submits that Watanabe does not make up for at least the above-discussed deficiencies of Ratnasingam.

Watanabe discloses, referring to FIG. 71, an image generator that "generates an image in which the inexecutable action ('lane change to right' 1202) is displayed in a display manner, different from the display manner of the other executable actions, where the icon indicating the inexecutable action is grayed out or the luminance of the icon is reduced":
FIG. 71

SVG {EMBED HERE} 2.333.063
ent information"
Watanabe, FIG. 71 (annotated) and [0597].

Watanabe further discloses that "there are start and end points of a lane end section within a predetermined distance, the distances to the start and end points of the lane end section are classified into a plurality of predetermined levels, and the numerical values of the classified levels are stored in the part of the 'distance to start/end point of lane end section'." Id. at [0392]. According to Watanabe, "[w]hen there are no start and end points of a lane end section within the predetermined distance, '0' is stored in the part of the 'distance to start/end point of lane end section'." Id.
That is, at best, Watanabe discloses classifying start and end points of a lane end section within a predetermined distance into a plurality of predetermined levels, and storing those levels.

The Office Action appears to equate the classifying of the start and end points of Watanabe to the claimed "distance information." See Office Action, p. 12. Even assuming for the sake of argument only that the Office Action's equation is otherwise appropriate or correct, which Applicant does not address, Watanabe still would not disclose, teach, or suggest "provide, through the information provision device to the driver, judgment information ... .comprising distance information from the current point to a point where the second lane is unable to be driven due to the at least one of the blockage or the ending of the second lane," as recited in Claim 1. Instead, at best, Watanabe discloses storing levels corresponding to the start and end points and is silent as to providing any such information to a driver.
Consequently, Watanabe does not disclose or suggest at least the cited features recited in Claim 1.

The Office Action does not allege that Abe discloses the above-identified features of Claim 1 nor does Abe make up for at least these deficiencies of Ratnasingam and Watanabe. Thus, even assuming for the sake of argument only that the proposed Ratnasingam-Abe-Watanabe
combination would have been proper, which Applicant does not concede, the proposed combination does not disclose, teach, or suggest all features recited in Claim 1.
In view of the above, Applicant respectfully submits that Claim 1 is patentable over the cited references and requests withdrawal of the rejection.

To the extent that independent Claims 6 and 7 recite features similar to the above-noted features of Claim 1, Applicant submits that Claims 6 and 7 are patentable for at least reasons similar to those discussed above with respect to Claim 1.

Applicant respectfully submits that dependent Claims 3 and 4 are patentable due to their respective dependencies, as well as for their additional features. This should not be construed as an acquiescence to Examiner's interpretation of the claims, or reading of those claim elements on the prior art, and Applicant expressly reserves the right to establish the patentability of those additional claim limitations, should the need arise.
Claim 5 is canceled by the present Amendment thus rendering moot its rejection. Conclusion

In view of the above, reconsideration and allowance of this application are now believed to be in order, and such actions are hereby solicited.
